usage.describe: Market-wide mechanisms that can move every sector: discount rates, liquidity, and flows from participants who are forced to buy or sell. Sector maps refer to these concepts instead of repeating them. All links are hypotheses to investigate.
usage.scope_rule: A concept belongs here when it explains who is forced to buy or sell, and why. Mathematical transforms of price history, such as RSI or moving-average crossovers, are not concepts; they belong to the evaluator.

unobservable_concepts.purpose: Concepts with observability proxy or none are kept so that mechanical causes stay in view when a fundamental lead fails.
unobservable_concepts.never_scored: A concept with observability none is never assessed as supported or contradicted. A report may only say it was not ruled out.
unobservable_concepts.not_a_default_explanation: Naming such a concept as the cause of a move requires stating what observation would have distinguished it from the alternatives.
unobservable_concepts.proxies_stay_named: A result conditioned on a proxy is a finding about the proxy. A trend-break result is about trend state, not trend-follower flows; a VIX/VIX3M result is about the term structure, not dealer gamma.

sector_node.describe: Stands for the broad US equity market. An edge targeting it suggests a market-wide exposure; whether it applies to a given sector or company must be reviewed.

branches.question: Are discount rates, real yields or system liquidity repricing all risk assets?
Are option dealers and volatility structures dampening moves or amplifying them?
Are trend-following, volatility-control or leveraged books near thresholds that force them to sell?

concepts.label: Fed Policy
concepts.description_lead: Sets the policy rate path and the size of the balance sheet

concepts.label: Real Yields
concepts.description_lead: Discount rate applied to long-duration equity cash flows
observables_to_research: 10-year real yield level and rate of change

concepts.label: Credit Spreads
concepts.description_lead: Price of corporate credit risk and a gauge of funding conditions

concepts.label: USD Liquidity
concepts.description_lead: Availability and cost of dollar funding
concepts.observable_with: No single series measures dollar funding stress. The dollar index, cross-currency basis and funding-rate spreads each capture part of it; reading any one as funding stress assumes the move is not driven by trade or rate differentials.

concepts.label: Volatility Term Structure
concepts.description_lead: Shape of implied volatility across maturities

concepts.label: Dealer Gamma
concepts.description_lead: Net option gamma held by dealers, which sets whether their hedging dampens or amplifies moves
observables_to_research: estimated net dealer gamma by strike
index level against the estimated gamma-flip level
concepts.observable_with: Dealer positions are not published. Daily option open interest by strike is public, and a gamma estimate can be built from it only by assuming which side dealers hold. Vendor estimates rest on the same assumption. The VIX/VIX3M ratio is not a measurement of dealer gamma.

concepts.label: Options Expiry Calendar
concepts.description_lead: Scheduled dates on which option positions and their hedges roll off
observables_to_research: open interest expiring on each date
share of volume in same-day-expiry options

concepts.label: Trend-Following Flows
concepts.description_lead: Systematic funds that cut or add exposure when medium-term price trends break
observables_to_research: leveraged-fund net positions in equity index futures
index level against medium-term trend levels
concepts.observable_with: Fund positions are not published. The CFTC's weekly Commitments of Traders report gives leveraged-fund positions in equity index futures, a wider group than trend followers, published with a lag of several days. A price crossing a moving average is the trigger these funds respond to, not a measurement of their selling.

concepts.label: Volatility-Control Flows
concepts.description_lead: Funds that scale equity exposure down as realised volatility rises
observables_to_research: realised volatility of the equity index, as the input these funds respond to
concepts.observable_with: No public data shows the positions or trades of volatility-targeting funds. Realised volatility is the input to their rule, not a measurement of their flows. This would need fund-level exposure disclosures or a prime-broker dataset.

concepts.label: Market Breadth
concepts.description_lead: How widely an index move is shared across its members
observables_to_research: share of index members above their 50-day and 200-day averages

concepts.label: Margin and ETF Flows
concepts.description_lead: Leverage in brokerage accounts and money moving through index funds
observables_to_research: ETF shares outstanding, creations and redemptions
concepts.observable_with: Margin debt is published monthly with a lag, too slowly to date a liquidation. ETF creations and redemptions are inferred from changes in shares outstanding. Neither shows forced selling directly; reading them that way assumes the change was involuntary.

concept_edges.mechanism_hypothesis: Changes in the expected policy path may move real yields.
Rapid rises in real yields may compress the valuation multiples of long-duration equities.
Widening credit spreads may tighten funding and pull money out of higher-beta stocks first, narrowing breadth.
Dollar funding stress may force holders of dollar-funded positions to sell risk assets.
Near-term implied volatility above three-month implied volatility indicates strong demand for short-dated protection.
Volatility spikes and term-structure inversion may coincide with dealers holding negative gamma. This needs independent positioning evidence; the term structure does not measure it.
Expiry removes option positions and their hedges, which may change the dealer gamma regime around those dates.
When dealers hold negative gamma, their delta hedging may sell into falls and buy into rises, amplifying moves.
Breaks of medium-term trends may trigger mechanical selling by trend-following funds.
A jump in realised volatility may force volatility-targeting funds to cut equity exposure.
An index move carried by few members, or a spike in correlation among members, indicates a fragile or crowded market.
Margin calls and fund redemptions may force selling that is unrelated to company fundamentals.
